card: Paper card. Question: How can single-phase refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) be designed to achieve ultrahigh yield strength at 1600°C, and what is the underlying deformation mechanism responsible for the observed plateau strength?. System: Hf0.5MoNbTaW and HfMoNbTaW refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs). Processing: Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization treatment at 2100°C for 2 hours with subsequent air cooling in an ultrahigh-temperature furnace under Ar flow. Test conditions: Compression testing at a strain rate of 10⁻³ 1/s from ambient temperature to 1600°C; samples were 3.6 mm in diameter and 6 mm in height for 1600°C tests. Findings: HfMoNbTaW alloy after homogenization exhibits a yield strength of 571 MPa at 1600°C, which is higher than MoNbTaVW (477 MPa).; A plateau of strength occurs from 800°C to 1200°C for HfMoNbTaW, with a value of approximately 950 MPa.; Homogenization at 2100°C for 2 h results in a homogeneous body-centered cubic (bcc) phase with no precipitation.; The theoretical yield strength (σycal) for HfMoNbTaW increases by 30.8% from 2393 MPa to 3131 MPa upon equiatomic addition of Hf into MoNbTaW.; The shear modulus of HfMoNbTaW was measured to be 73 ± 1 GPa via nanoindentation.; Extrapolation of high-temperature strength data suggests a room temperature strength of 4536 MPa, consistent with edge dislocation control calculations (4206 MPa).; Adding Hf to MoNbTaW increases yield strength by 47.5% compared to MoNbTaW (1561 MPa vs 1058 MPa).. Mechanism: The authors propose that the plateau strength and ultrahigh elevated-temperature strength result from a transition in the deformation mode from screw dislocations to edge dislocations. Below the critical temperature (Tc), strength decreases due to thermal activation of screw dislocations. Above Tc, edge dislocations become dominant in general yielding, leading to a plateau in strength and high strength at elevated temperatures.. Limitations: The text notes that the theoretical yield strength calculated using the average shear modulus (Gmix) is generally larger than the experimental value, and that the assumption of mixed dislocation control (α=9) was an overestimate compared to screw dislocation control (α=2) at low temperatures.. Future work: The authors state that a similar alloy design strategy could be applied to develop more RHEAs with an ultrahigh strength level.. Quote: "HfMoNbTaW alloy exhibits a yield strength of 571 MPa at 1600°C, much higher than that of MoNbTaVW (477 MPa)."

card: Paper card. Question: How to achieve a simultaneous balance of high fracture strength and high ductility in high-entropy alloys while overcoming inferior castability and compositional segregation?. System: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA). Processing: Vacuum induction melting of commercially pure elements (Al, Co, Ni: 99.9 wt.%; Cr, Fe: 99.5 ~ 99.6 wt.%) in a BN crucible; heating to 600°C for 1 hour; pouring at 1500°C into a MgO crucible (220 mm length, 62 mm upper ID, 50 mm bottom ID) under argon atmosphere (0.06 MPa); bulk ingot weight ~2.5 kg.. Test conditions: Room temperature tensile tests at strain rate 1 × 10−3 s−1; elevated temperature tests at 600°C and 700°C at strain rate 1 × 10−3 s−1; cold rolling with 8% thickness reduction followed by tensile testing at 2 × 10−3 s−1.. Findings: The as-cast alloy exhibited a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure with an inter-lamellar spacing of about 2 μm.; Room temperature tensile test showed a fracture stress of 944 MPa and an elongation of 25.6%.; The proof stress was 75 MPa, while the fracture stress reached close to 1.2 GPa (true stress condition).; At 600°C, the alloy maintained a fracture stress of 806 MPa and elongation of 33.7%.; At 700°C, the alloy maintained a fracture stress of 538 MPa and elongation of 22.9%.; Cold rolling with 8% reduction increased the true fracture stress to 1265 MPa while maintaining 9.9% elongation.; The density of the EHEA was measured to be 7.38 g/cm3.; The ratio of fracture strength to proof stress (σUTS/σ0.2) was close to 16.. Mechanism: The authors attribute the unprecedented strain hardening and balanced properties to the fine regular lamellar structure that easily stores dislocations and the alternating soft fcc phases and hard B2-structured NiAl-rich phases. When dislocations pass through soft fcc phases, the hard B2 phases, including nanoscale precipitates, pin the movement of dislocations resulting in significant work hardening.. Limitations: The text notes that the mechanism for the low elastic limit (proof stress) is still unclear at this stage.. Future work: Further exploration of new EHEAs will be based on physical metallurgy principles using atomic radius, mixing enthalpy, and valence electron concentration; thermodynamics calculations based on the CALPHAD method can provide guidance once reliable databases are established; the potential for producing ultrahigh strength components after large plastic deformation awaits further investigations.. Quote: "To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases."

card: Paper card. Question: How does a novel refractory high entropy alloy (NV1) behave under long-term isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C and 1100 °C, and what is the mechanism governing its oxidation resistance over 200 hours?. System: NV1 alloy (Al, Cr, Mo, Nb, Si, Ta, Ti; designed based on CrMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr with reduced Ti, removed Zr, and added Al, Si, increased Cr). Processing: Cold crucible levitation melting of high purity elemental raw materials (>99.9 wt%) to cast a 1.1 kg cone-shaped ingot; samples machined by electrical discharge machining and ground to 1200 grit; isothermal oxidation performed in flowing dry air using a thermogravimetric analyser (SETARAM TAG 24-18S) and muffle furnace. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C and 1100 °C for up to 200 hours in flowing dry air; microstructural characterization performed at intervals of 1, 12, 40, 50, 100, and 200 hours. Findings: At 1000 °C, the mass gain after 200 hours was 6.53 mg/cm2, following an exponential dependence throughout the entire duration.; At 1100 °C, the mass gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm2, which is lower than at 1000 °C, showing three stages of parabolic dependence.; The external oxide layer at both temperatures consisted primarily of a CrTaO4-based oxide with dispersed Al2O3 and Cr2O3.; At 1000 °C, the CrTaO4-based oxide layer was porous with large volume defects due to insufficient kinetics, preventing it from acting as an effective barrier.; At 1100 °C, the CrTaO4-based oxide layer was denser and more continuous, leading to controlled oxidation and reduced weight gain.; TiN particles (size ~1.5 μm) formed preferentially within the Mo-rich dendritic regions at both temperatures, while Al2O3 formed in the internal oxidation depth.; The CrTaO4-based oxide at 1100 °C contained up to 7 at% Al and 2.2 at% less Cr compared to the oxide formed at 1000 °C, indicating non-stoichiometric substitution.. Mechanism: At 1000 °C, insufficient kinetics prevented the formation of a dense, protective CrTaO4 layer, leading to heterogeneous oxidation, volume defects, and exponential weight gain driven by external oxidation and nitridation. At 1100 °C, enhanced diffusion kinetics allowed for the homogeneous growth of a denser, continuous CrTaO4-based layer that acted as a barrier to oxygen and element diffusion, resulting in parabolic weight gain; however, Mo evaporation at the oxide/substrate interface in Stage II temporarily accelerated oxidation before Stage III saw further CrTaO4 formation.. Limitations: The study notes that while CrTaO4-based oxide provided protection, it could not fully prevent the ingestion of oxygen and nitrogen, leading to internal oxidation and nitridation over the long duration.. Future work: The authors propose that the nature of the CrTaO4-based oxide needs to be carefully examined in future studies, and that the influence of nitridation on RHEA properties is an important subject for further investigation.. Quote: "At 1100 °C, mass gain curve showed two parabolic dependences associated with the formation of protective CrTaO4-based oxide layer and the weight gain after 200 hours was 4.03 mg/cm2"

card: Paper card. Question: Can nanocrystalline high-entropy rare-earth hexaboride (HEReB6) ceramics be fabricated to achieve combined structural and functional performance, specifically high mechanical properties and superior thermionic emission, suitable for extreme environments?. System: (La0.25Ce0.25Nd0.25Eu0.25)B6 (HEReB6-1) and individual binary rare-earth hexaborides (LaB6, CeB6, NdB6, EuB6). Processing: Solid-state reaction of La2O3, CeO2, Nd2O3, Eu2O3, and NaBH4 at 1,373 K for 30 min to synthesize nanopowders; followed by high-pressure sintering of nanopowders at 6 GPa and 1,473–1,773 K for 5 min to fabricate bulk ceramics. Test conditions: Mechanical tests (Vickers hardness, fracture toughness) from room temperature to 1,073 K; electrical resistivity from 200 to 320 K; thermionic emission current density measured in vacuum (< 5 × 10−5 Pa) at 1,673 K, 1,773 K, and 1,873 K. Findings: Relative density of 96.3 ± 2.2% achieved with a nanoscale grain size of 94 ± 28 nm at a sintering temperature of 1,673 K.; Vickers hardness of 23.4 ± 0.4 GPa and elastic modulus of 261 ± 13 GPa at room temperature, exceeding the average values of the four individual ReB6 samples (18.3 GPa and 232 GPa, respectively).; Fracture toughness of 3.0 ± 0.2 MPa•m1/2 at room temperature, slightly higher than the average of the four individual ReB6 samples (2.7 MPa•m1/2).; Electrical resistivity of HEReB6-1 was greater than the average value of the four individual ReB6 samples across the measured temperature range.; Maximum emission current density reached 48.3 A•cm−2 at 1,873 K, significantly higher than polycrystalline ReB6 samples.; Effective work function (Φe) of 2.83 eV at 1,873 K, which was slightly lower than the average values of the four individual ReB6 cathodes.; The (001) fiber texture was identified as the major texture orientation in the nanocrystalline microstructure.. Mechanism: The superior mechanical properties are attributed to solid-solution and grain-refinement strengthening effects, along with nanoscale crack-deflection and grain-bridging toughening mechanisms. The high electrical resistivity results from exacerbated electron scattering due to severe lattice distortion. The remarkable thermionic emission performance is primarily attributed to the presence of the (001) fiber texture, which exposes surfaces with the lowest work function, and the contribution of d-orbital electrons from rare-earth elements (particularly Nd) to the conduction band.. Limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.. Future work: The authors propose that this work will open up a new research field on HEReB6 ceramics with potential applications in thermionic emission cathodes.. Quote: "The results showed that the samples possessed outstanding comprehensive mechanical properties and a high electrical resistivity from room temperature to high temperatures"
W4224434693.title: Nanocrystalline high-entropy hexaboride ceramics enable remarkable performance as thermionic emission cathodes

card: Paper card. Question: How does entropy stabilization in transition-metal-based high entropy oxides (TM-HEO) influence reversible lithium storage capacity, cycling stability, and the underlying reaction mechanism compared to medium entropy oxides?. System: Transition-metal-based high entropy oxides (TM-HEO) with composition (Co0.2Cu0.2Mg0.2Ni0.2Zn0.2)O; compared to 4-cation medium entropy oxides (MEO) such as (Co0.25Cu0.25Zn0.25Ni0.25)O and (Co0.25Cu0.25Mg0.25Zn0.25)O. Processing: Nebulized Spray Pyrolysis (NSP) at 1150 °C; 4-cation systems required post-annealing at 1000 °C for 1 h under ambient atmosphere; electrodes cast with 63 wt% active material, 22 wt% Super C65, 15 wt% PVA binder. Test conditions: Galvanostatic cycling in Li-metal coin cells, voltage range 0.01–3 V vs. Li+/Li, specific currents from 50 to 3000 mA g−1, room temperature, 1 M LiPF6 in EC/DMC or EC/EMC electrolyte. Findings: The 5-cation TM-HEO cycled over 300 cycles at 200 mA g−1 with specific capacities stabilizing around 650 mAh g−1 after initial activation.; The 5-cation system achieved a specific capacity of 770 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles following a rate increase to 3 A g−1 for 5 cycles.; Medium entropy oxides (4-cation systems) showed rapid capacity degradation, with the Co-removed variant failing completely after ~10 cycles.; The Coulombic efficiency of the 5-cation TM-HEO stabilized between 99.4% and 99.95% in the range of cycles 60–400.; The 4-cation system without Zn (TM-MEO(-Zn)) exhibited a two-step oxidation process at 1.7 V and 2.2 V, unlike the single-step oxidation of the 5-cation system.; High-loading electrodes (2.3 mg cm−2) maintained Coulombic efficiencies >98.5% and an areal capacity of 1.3 mAh cm−2 after 30 cycles.; No metallic phases or Cu dendrites were detected via TEM/EDX after 100 cycles, despite the conversion reaction mechanism.. Mechanism: The authors propose that the rock-salt structure is preserved as a permanent host matrix during the entire conversion process. While some cations (e.g., Co, Cu) are reduced to metallic states during lithiation, they remain 'trapped' within the defect-rich rock-salt lattice stabilized by unreduced cations (e.g., Mg, Ni). This entropy stabilization lowers the Gibbs free energy, favoring the re-incorporation of reduced cations into the original lattice sites upon delithiation, preventing phase separation and structural collapse.. Limitations: The theoretical capacity cannot be predicted with high accuracy due to unknown additional processes like Zn-Li alloying or intermetallic formation; some 4-cation systems (TM-MEO(-Mg) and TM-MEO(-Ni)) could not be synthesized as single-phase compounds even at high temperatures.. Future work: Further investigations should be pursued to explore the full potential of high entropy oxide electrode materials, including the addition of other cations (Fe, Mn, Cr, V) to develop a modular method for tailoring electrodes to specific needs.. Quote: "The stabilization effect of entropy brings significant benefits for the storage capacity retention of high entropy oxides and greatly improves the cycling stability."
W2888579709.title: High entropy oxides for reversible energy storage

card: Paper card. Question: Can high-entropy solid solutions be formed in non-oxide ceramic metal diborides with a hexagonal layered structure, and do they exhibit superior hardness and oxidation resistance compared to their constituent individual diborides?. System: Seven equimolar five-component metal diborides: (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Mo0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Mo0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Mo0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Mo0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2, (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Cr0.2Ti0.2)B2, and (Hf0.2Zr0.2W0.2Mo0.2Ti0.2)B2. Processing: High-energy ball milling (HEBM) for 6 hours in WC media with 60-minute milling/5-minute cooling cycles, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 2000 °C for 5 minutes under 30 MPa pressure in vacuum (10^-2 Torr). Test conditions: Hardness measured via Vickers indentation at 200 kgf/mm2 with 15s hold time; oxidation resistance assessed via sequential isothermal annealing in flowing dry air at 800–1500 °C for 1 hour per step. Findings: Six of the seven compositions formed a single-phase hexagonal AlB2 structure with greater than 92% of theoretical density.; Aberration-corrected STEM confirmed 2-D high-entropy metal layers separated by rigid boron nets with no detectable layered segregation along the c-axis.; The measured standard deviations of lattice spacings between basal (0001) planes were only ~0.6% of the average c lattice parameter.; Hardness of the high-entropy diborides was generally greater than the average hardness of the five individual constituent metal diborides.; Oxidation resistance was generally better than the average of individual components, with HEB#1 and HEB#7 maintaining shape at 1500 °C while TiB2 pulverized.; Revised Hume-Rothery size-difference factors based on lattice constants (δc) of 3.9% to 5.2% rationalized single-phase formation, whereas the non-single-phase specimen had δc ≈ 6.2%.; Minor secondary oxide phases ((Zr, Hf)O2) were observed in six specimens, and a secondary (Ti1.6W2.4)B4 phase was found in the W-containing specimen.. Mechanism: The formation of high-entropy solid solutions is rationalized by a revised Hume-Rothery size-difference factor calculated from lattice constants rather than atomic radii; the rigid 2-D boron net constrains the metal layers, reducing the effective size mismatch (δa) and allowing entropy stabilization of the disordered solid solution despite larger atomic size differences in the c-direction.. Limitations: The presence of porosity and oxide inclusions resulting from the HEBM procedure adversely affected hardness and oxidation resistance; MoB2 is metastable at room temperature and W2B5 starting powder has limited solubility; the study did not fully optimize microstructure for maximum property performance.. Future work: Further systematic investigation of hardness, oxidation resistance, and other properties is needed, particularly focusing on processing optimization to achieve fully-dense and oxide-free specimens and utilizing the large compositional design space to tailor protective oxide scales.. Quote: "Greater than 92% of the theoretical densities have been generally achieved with largely uniform compositions from nanoscale to microscale."
